brief.destination: CallerSignal presents an immediately understandable, uncertainty-honest risk state and has a lawful source-intake foundation without scraping or republishing unlicensed caller databases.
brief.problem: The current web result makes source confidence visually dominant and the product has no durable source-rights registry, which risks users reading numbering confidence as safety and maintainers treating public caller-report sites as freely reusable data.
brief.chosen_approach: Adopt a hybrid reputation model: present four calibrated risk states across shared contracts and the web; use only official, licensed, or first-party moderated evidence; record source rights before ingestion; never treat missing reports, lookup volume, or a displayed number as proof of safety, guilt, or identity.
non_goals: Scrape, copy, or republish third-party caller-report databases without explicit documented permission.
Ingest real phone numbers, call histories, free-text accusations, or requester identities into the public repository.
Describe no matching reports as proof that answering or returning a call is safe.
Implement public community report ingestion before legal, privacy, moderation, retention, correction, deletion, and abuse controls are approved.

work_units.summary: Adopt the hybrid reputation vision and safety gates
acceptance: The repo-local and public vision contracts define the four calibrated risk states and the official/licensed/first-party evidence boundary without introducing a safe-number promise.
The agent spec defines shared CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web behavior, representative evaluations, fail-closed behavior, and metadata-only production observability.
The source-rights registry becomes a dependency of report ingestion, and the new work is placed in dependency order under the product hierarchy.

work_units.summary: Define four calibrated risk states in the shared result contract
acceptance: Every canonical lookup exposes exactly one risk state: official_warning, elevated_signals, no_risk_evidence, or insufficient_evidence, with stable reason codes and an explicit action message.

Current numbering evidence alone produces no_risk_evidence only in the narrow sense that no risk evidence was found, while stale, failed, contradictory, or unsupported coverage produces insufficient_evidence.
No risk state can be raised by lookup popularity or one unverified report, and all existing CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web consumers remain schema-valid.
verification: uv run pytest tests/unit/test_assessment.py tests/integration/test_lookup.py tests/integration/test_cli.py tests/integration/test_mcp.py tests/integration/test_http_api.py -q

work_units.summary: Render an HIBP-inspired risk result without false safety claims
acceptance: The result leads with a large text-and-icon risk banner whose wording and visual treatment distinguish all four states without relying on color alone.
Source confidence is visually subordinate to the risk state and cannot be mistaken for a safety percentage.
Desktop and mobile proof confirms no clipping, overlap, overflow, unreadable contrast, placeholder text, or console errors, and the live Vercel alias serves the verified result.

work_units.summary: Create a machine-validated source-rights registry and intake gate
acceptance: Every enabled source records authority, stable URL, evidence class, reuse basis, permitted fields, freshness, outage behavior, and whether personal or free-text data is allowed.
Third-party caller-report sites without explicit permission are recorded as disabled permission-required candidates with zero permitted ingestion fields and no copied records.
The registry and documentation make robots permission, copyright/database rights, privacy review, takedown, and provenance separate gates before any adapter can be enabled.
